title: PreDAC: An Efficient Framework of Pre-Refining Enhanced Design Space Exploration for Approximate Computing
problem: Design Space Exploration (DSE) algorithms for approximate computing face challenges obtaining optimal solutions within large and complex design spaces efficiently.
motivation: Approximate computing offers significant energy-efficiency gains; efficient DSE algorithms are needed to optimize accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs within reasonable time.
method: The framework starts by applying application-specific rules to reduce the design space (the set of possible design choices) before the main search. This pre-refinement step is much faster than exploring the entire original space and shrinks what the main search must evaluate. The main search then uses a cost-performance formula (customized per application) to find the best design by weighing tradeoffs between efficiency and accuracy.
key_novelty: This work combines a pre-refinement step that shrinks the design space for each application with a cost-performance-based algorithm to find the best design option.
contributions: Pre-refining framework providing application-customized design space and cost-performance formula
Cost-performance-based DSE algorithm leveraging pre-refined space
87x speedup in DSE with 23% hardware overhead improvement; additional 7.7x acceleration and 8.8% optimization vs. advanced frameworks
